sources.citation: Gopalakrishnan, N. [c. 2011-13; archive.org upload 2023]. Churahi. In: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India, Linguistic Survey of India: Himachal Pradesh, pp. 120-175.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Sec. 2.1.2 'Suprasegmental phonemes' (p. 124): 'In Churahi Length and Nasalization are realized with long vowels' -- only length and nasalization listed; sec. 2.4 Syllable (pp. 146-149) gives CV templates only; no token 'stress', 'accent', 'tone' or 'pitch' anywhere in the chapter.

sources.citation: Bailey, T. Grahame. 1920 [1915]. Linguistic Studies from the Himalayas. Asiatic Society Monographs XVIII. London: Royal Asiatic Society.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Curahi is mentioned only for r-dropping in bolnu / kahnu / manu (Rohru chapter); no Curahi accent statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page chur1258 (classification refs: Grierson 1916; Campbell et al. 2022; van Driem 2007); Wikipedia 'Churahi language' (refs: Ethnologue 25, ELP, census tables only).
sources.note: No descriptive references beyond Grierson/Bailey/Tobdan; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. 1916. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX Indo-Aryan Family, Central Group, Part IV: Specimens of the Pahari Languages and Gujuri. Calcutta: Superintendent of Government Printing. 'Churahi', pp. 817-846.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. 'Pronunciation' paragraph (p. 821) covers only epenthesis (khata / fem. khaiti), an 'indefinite' vowel scale, loss of aspiration, hardening of sonants, r-elision and r-insertion; no accent or stress remark in the Churahi section (sketch is 'mainly based on Mr. Bailey's excellent work').

sources.citation: Bailey, T. Grahame. 1908. The Languages of the Northern Himalayas, being studies in the grammar of twenty-six Himalayan dialects. London: Royal Asiatic Society. Part III (Chamba dialects; dated Wazirabad, 30 Jan 1903): Introduction pp. i-vi; 'Curahi' pp. 27-38.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent for Curahi. The only accent remarks in the Chamba part concern other dialects: Bhateali stative participles in -ada have 'the accent on the antepenultimate' (p. ii) and in Bhateali/Cameali post-vocalic h 'raises the tone of the syllable' (p. ii). The Curahi grammar (pp. 27-38) is nouns, pronouns, verbs, vocabulary, numerals, sentences; pronunciation notes limited to 'mata (pronounced mat")' (p. 32) and 'sat-hatthar' (p. 36).
